name: Blooms
description: Nick Bentley's colourful Go-like game on a hexagonal board: place one or two stones of different colours, and capture every enemy bloom you fence in.
rules: Blooms is played on a hexagonal board (5 cells per side here; 4 and 6 are variants). Player 1 owns red and yellow stones, player 2 blue and black.
A bloom is a connected group of stones of one colour (a lone stone counts). A bloom is fenced when no empty cell touches any of its stones.
Player 1 starts by placing one stone of either of their colours. After that, on your turn you place one or two stones on empty cells; two stones must be of different colours. You may place just one.

When your turn ends, you capture every fenced enemy bloom (removing it and counting its stones). Your own fenced blooms are not captured on your turn; they stay until the end of your opponent's turn, so a fenced bloom of yours can still be freed — or captured.
The first player to capture the target number of enemy stones wins: 20 on this board (15 on base 4, 25 on base 6). Sacrificing stones to set up a bigger capture is the heart of the game.
Interpretation: the game is drawn or decided on captures after 500 plies.
